paper.title: CPGA: Coding Priors-Guided Aggregation Network for Compressed Video Quality Enhancement
paper.page_convention: 1-based PDF pages; printed page 2964 is PDF p.1

text_evidence_sources: Rendered PDF pages and verified crops

claims.claim: Codec priors have separate temporal and spatial roles.

evidence.note: Architecture and input paths directly show roles.

caveats: Codec vectors are not necessarily true optical flow.

claims.claim: VCP supplies 300 clips with extracted HEVC priors.

evidence.note: 300 clips, 48 frames each, LDB/RA and four QPs.

caveats: Coverage of other codecs not established.

claims.claim: Temporal aggregation gates features using target correlation with prediction and motion-warped features.

evidence.note: Formula transcription verified against rendered PDF.

caveats: Softmax axis not explicit in text.

claims.claim: NLAU uses weighted pooled context rather than full all-pairs attention.

evidence.note: The matrix products have dimensions 1×HW and HW×C.

caveats: The pooled vector compresses spatial information.

claims.claim: CPGA improves average LDB fidelity over STDR by 0.02–0.03 dB.
caveats: Does not win every sequence or metric.

claims.claim: RA improvement over STDR is 0.02–0.05 dB.
Combining priors improves the ablation result from 0.69 to 0.82 dB.

evidence.note: Single priors and combinations improve the displayed gains.

caveats: Prose single-prior gains disagree with table.

claims.claim: VCP training improves CPGA by 0.03 dB over MFQE-CP.
caveats: Other methods MFQE numbers come from their papers.

claims.claim: CPGA is faster than STDR but not RFDA in the table.
caveats: End-to-end extraction and buffering breakdown absent.

claims.claim: Temporal perceptual smoothness is not established by the short PSNR plot.
caveats: No temporal perceptual metric or user study.

claims.claim: Selected crops visually support reduced compression damage.

evidence.note: Compare GT, compressed and enhanced crops.

caveats: Selected qualitative examples cannot establish preference rate.

claims.claim: Future-frame context entails a latency caveat.
caveats: Inference about buffering, not a measured latency result.
